proposed.rationale: LEARNINGS ##46 set the category budget at 12 because 20 year-bars produced 19 collisions. Relaxing it to 24 lets that defect back in; the probe measures whether the task set still sees it.
an off-by-one relaxation: if 12 were too tight, one extra category would recover a refusal at no legibility cost. The probe asks whether any task can tell the two budgets apart.

the row budget is one row tighter than the measured collision boundary: 41 unpivotable rows render with 0 collisions and 42 produce 41. If that holds on the task set, the budget refuses a table it could draw.
one row past the measured boundary: it admits the 48-row table, whose tick labels collide. The expected verdict is a rejection, so this is the negative control for 'any relaxation is a gain'.

LEARNINGS ##47 records the row budget as a refusal that was nearly a regression. Relaxing it to 60 re-admits the 48-row table and tests whether the collisions it was protecting against are still there.

NEGATIVE CONTROL. The baseline reproduces its reference exactly (distance 0.0000), so a +0.5 uniform shift measures 0.0590 -- a regression. A loop that selects this cannot tell an improvement from a perturbation.
NEGATIVE CONTROL, further out. +1.0 measures 0.0590 as well; the two together show the penalty is flat in this direction, so neither can be picked by accident.
